intro: Morocco sits at the north-west corner of Africa, just across a narrow strait from Europe. It is one of the world's oldest monarchies.

chapters.title: Amazigh and Romans
text: At Jebel Irhoud, scientists found the oldest known fossils of Homo sapiens, about 300,000 years old. Amazigh (Berber) peoples have lived here for thousands of years. Phoenicians traded on the coast and Rome ruled the north, leaving ruins at Volubilis.

chapters.title: Islamic dynasties
text: Arabs brought Islam around 700. The Idrisids founded Fez, home to al-Qarawiyyin, often called the oldest continuously operating university in the world, founded in 859 by Fatima al-Fihri.

Amazigh dynasties, the Almoravids and Almohads, ruled empires stretching into Spain. Marrakesh and later Meknes became royal cities. The Alaouite dynasty, which still reigns, came to power in the 1600s.

highlight.title: Al-Qarawiyyin
highlight.text: It was founded by a woman, Fatima al-Fihri, in 859.

chapters.title: Protectorate and independence
text: In 1912 France and Spain divided Morocco into protectorates. It became independent in 1956 under King Mohammed V. In 1975 Morocco took control of most of Western Sahara, a territory whose status is still disputed.
King Mohammed VI has reigned since 1999. A 2023 earthquake in the Atlas killed nearly 3,000 people.
